name: Define a bundle (components and quantities)
trigger: The operator wants to sell a set that OpenLinker reserves, routes and packs from its components.
preconditions: The bundle exists as an OpenLinker catalogue variant, which today can only come from a master sync (C-061).
Every component is a synced, non-stale variant.
Pilot assumption: one warehouse (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 0).
mainFlow: The operator opens the bundle variant and adds components, each a variant with a whole quantity per set.
OpenLinker validates: positive whole quantities, no self-reference, no component that is itself a bundle, no stale component.
OpenLinker shows warnings, not refusals, when a component VAT rate differs from the bundle rate (B-14) or when the bundle variant is a master kit that keeps its own stock (B-03, B-20).
OpenLinker refuses a definition on a variant that is a WooCommerce bundle container (B-05 guard).
OpenLinker stores the component set with a definition version.
OpenLinker recomputes the bundle availability and enqueues a propagation for the bundle variant (B-02).
altFlows: Edit: a new definition version is stored; orders already ingested keep their frozen expansion (B-10).
Remove a component: new version; open orders are not changed.
A component later becomes stale: the bundle becomes unsellable (B-02), the definition stays.
The operator tries to nest a bundle: refused in v1 (B-26).

In-set price per component (spike D3a): not entered in the pilot. The sources support a split computed at sale time from each component own selling price as the default, with a typed in-set price only as an override carrying a recorded reason (verify/bundle-price-split.md section 4). A share above the standalone price raises a warning; capping is not itself an accepted method (BFH XI R 22/22, r5/8-tax-fiscal.md C-035).
The same component listed twice in one recipe: merged into one component row with the summed quantity, so the component id stays unique (verify/component-line-id.md surprise 4).

channelData.Others: Subiekt GT/nexo komplet `Skladniki` (r4/phase1/3-pl-saas-and-erp.md section 4). Not read by the bridge.

olBehaviour: Core only: a new OpenLinker-owned definition table plus admin CRUD (the filed #3607 scope, r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 6). No adapter change, no new capability. The definition is the authority; channel or master compositions are never imported as truth in the pilot.

acceptance.then: the definition is stored as version 1 and the availability of B is recomputed from A and C

acceptance.then: the save is refused with a "nested bundles are not supported" reason

priorityReason: Every other Stage 1 bundle behaviour reads the definition; Stage 1 itself is conditional on the pilot client selling OL-packed kits on routed channels (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 8).
risks: Without an in-set price (deferred D3a), component documents and component returns have no price basis for pilot orders; mitigation is to freeze component catalogue gross prices in the expansion row (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 7.4).
An OpenLinker-only bundle variant has no source (C-061), so the bundle must exist as a product in the master.

The no-nesting rule is justified on cost only: "every competitor forbids nesting" is false (Cin7 supports multi-level assemblies; the BaseLinker quote was misattributed) (verify/nested-and-gift-stockout.md; Subiekt GT allows a komplet inside a komplet, r4/phase1/3-pl-saas-and-erp.md section 4.1).

The spike D3a "in-set price fixed at definition" conflicts with the price-split evidence, which favours a split at sale time by current standalone prices; a fixed figure goes stale as catalogue prices move (verify/bundle-price-split.md sections 3-4).

name: Bundle availability from components, published to channels; shared components
actor: System (availability and propagation); operator reads the result
trigger: A component stock write, an OpenLinker hold claimed or closed, a component marked stale, or a definition change.
preconditions: A bundle definition exists (B-01).
The bundle variant has at least one offer or shop-product mapping.
mainFlow: A component position is written; `InventoryService.setInventory` enqueues a propagation for that component (inventory.service.ts:96-121, r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md b1).
A reverse lookup "component -> bundles containing it" enqueues one propagation per bundle variant.

`IAvailabilityService` answers the bundle as min over components of floor(global ATP of component / quantity per set), from unbuffered global component answers; any unknown component makes the bundle unknown; the bundle variant own positions are ignored (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md b2).
The channel buffer and zero threshold are applied once, to the bundle number, by the existing write-back (inventory-sync.service.ts:99).
The freshness token for the bundle offer is the latest `updatedAt` over its components (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md b4).
The bundle offer quantity is written to each channel.
altFlows: A shared component is sold on its own: both the component offer and every bundle containing it are republished.

A component is stale: the bundle publishes 0 and the stale pause, its hourly sweep and the propagation stale guard all expand to bundles (stale-offer-pause.service.ts:90-104, offer-mapping.repository.ts:754-776).
A component has no positions: known 0 for that component, so the bundle is 0.
A component answer is unknown: the bundle publish is suppressed, never written as 0.

channelData.PrestaShop: The OL adapter already derives pack quantity on the read side (`derivePackAvailability`, prestashop-pack.types.ts:211-232) and reports it as the pack position (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md c1).

channelData.Shoper: Set availability follows components on the shop side; whether REST returns a derived number or a manual cap for the set is unknown (r4/phase1/3-pl-saas-and-erp.md section 1.3).

channelData.Others: Competitors: BaseLinker min of components, summing across warehouses is an option since 03/2025 (r5/4-competitors-pl.md C-039); Apilo recomputes every 15 min (C-041); Shopify is location-blind (r5/5-competitors-global.md).

acceptance.then: the buffer is subtracted once from the bundle figure, not per component

risks: Per-location availability for routing and global availability for publishing can disagree on a multi-warehouse install (Shopify shows the trap, r5/5-competitors-global.md); fine for a one-warehouse pilot.
The #2617 freshness guard refuses a bundle write if the token is taken from the triggering component instead of the max over components (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md b4).
Two routes to zero (stale pause and derived ATP) must agree (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md b5).

The stress test rates a missing recompute trigger as the top critical hole: without the reverse fan-out the kit offer keeps its old quantity until something touches the kit variant (verify/standard-stress-test.md A1).
BaseLinker sources disagree on summing across warehouses (help FAQ vs 03/2025 changelog, r5/4-competitors-pl.md C-039).

name: Pre-built kit with its own stock versus a virtual bundle
trigger: A kit is physically assembled and shelved and the master counts it as its own item.
preconditions: The master reports a stock figure for the kit itself (Subiekt komplet, PrestaShop pack in pack-only mode).
mainFlow: Master sync reports the kit as an ordinary variant with its own stock.
With no OpenLinker definition, the kit is handled as an ordinary product (works today).
If an OpenLinker definition is also saved on that variant, OpenLinker warns that the master keeps kit stock (pilot guard, r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 5).
Later: the master declares the kit stock mode as a three-state product fact and OpenLinker chooses virtual, own or both per bundle.
altFlows: Subiekt GT komplet not yet assembled ("Zmontuj"): the bridge publishes SUM(st_Stan) = 0 although components are on the shelf (C-022).
PrestaShop pack with `pack_stock_type=0` is read as "shop default" up to 9.1.x and fixed in 9.2.0, so OL can disagree with the shop on 9.2+ (r5/2-shops-erp.md section 3).
Cin7-style kitting: pick the assembled kit if in stock, else its components (r5/5-competitors-global.md CN3); later.

name: Order arrives as the parent only and is expanded
trigger: An order line names a set as one item: Allegro productSet offer, PrestaShop pack row, Erli, Amazon, Kaufland, or Shoper while children are ignored.
preconditions: The channel line resolves to an OpenLinker variant through offer or identifier mapping.
That variant has a bundle definition (B-01).
mainFlow: The adapter emits the line as it does today: one line, the channel line id, the bundle price.
Item resolution maps it 1:1 to the bundle variant (order-ingestion.service.ts:584-602).
Core recognises a bundle because the resolved variant has a definition; no adapter field is needed.
Core freezes the expansion for this order line (B-10).
Reservation, routing and sale decrement use the component lines from the expansion (B-23).
The order line, order snapshot, documents and channel writebacks keep the bundle line (D3).
altFlows: Unmapped line: the whole order stays `awaiting_mapping`, visibly (C-053).
Allegro sends `productSet` but no OL definition exists: later, an attention state "set sold, contents unknown in OpenLinker" (r5/1-allegro-pl.md section 3A).

Allegro `productSet` count or quantities differ from the OL definition: later, a drift attention, never an automatic re-definition (r5/1-allegro-pl.md section 3A, r5/3-marketplaces-countries.md C-027).

Allegro One Fulfillment set (`fulfilledBySource`): routing is skipped (#3636, order-ingestion.service.ts:1273); whether that short-circuit runs before the expansion and also skips component holds is unverified (r5/1-allegro-pl.md item 10, verify/standard-stress-test.md A14).

A definition created after the order was first ingested: the order must not be expanded on a later poll, because holds or work already exist on the bundle line id; the first ready ingestion records which line ids were evaluated (verify/standard-stress-test.md A2, see B-10).
PrestaShop pack sold in the PrestaShop shop itself: not routed (own-shop skip, fulfillment-routing-eligibility.types.ts:48-50); see B-20.

The OL mapper reads `offer.id`, `quantity`, `price`, name, tax only and ignores `productSet` and `offer.external.id` (C-002, allegro-order-source.adapter.ts:998-1016).

name: Order arrives as parent and children; no double counting
trigger: A shop sends a container line plus one line per component (WooCommerce bundle plugins; Shoper `children` if read).
preconditions: The source adapter emits child lines as ordinary order lines.
mainFlow: Pilot: OpenLinker refuses to save an OL definition on a variant that is a WooCommerce bundle container, so container and children are never both expanded (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 5).
Later: the adapter tags child lines with a three-state parent link, or a per-connection operator setting states "this source sends children as lines" (X-03).
Later: core treats tagged children as the expansion (or suppresses them when they match the definition exactly, the Linnworks Magento guard) and takes the price from whichever side carries it (B-19).
altFlows: WPC fixed price: parent carries the price, children are 0; WPC auto price: parent 0 with no tax, children carry discounted prices (r4/phase1/2-own-shops.md section 3).
Two identical bundles in one WPC order cannot be told apart reliably (link by product id, not order item id) (r4/phase1/2-own-shops.md section 3).
A WooCommerce grouped product arrives as independent lines with no parent: not a bundle for OL (r4/phase1/2-own-shops.md section 2.2).

name: Multipack: one offer equals N units of one product
actor: System (order ingestion); operator maps the offer
trigger: An Allegro multipack offer (productSet with one product, quantity N) is bought.
preconditions: The multipack offer is mapped to an OL bundle variant defined as {A x N} (B-01).
mainFlow: The order line arrives as one line, quantity q.
Core recognises the bundle variant (B-04) and freezes the expansion A x (q * N).
Reservation, routing and sale decrement act on A (B-23); the bench asks the packer for q * N units of A.
altFlows: The multipack offer is mapped (by hand or by barcode linking on the shared product EAN) to the single-unit variant A instead of a bundle: OL would reserve and decrement q units instead of q * N (inference, unverified live; the stress test rates it HIGH, verify/standard-stress-test.md A5; the BaseLinker case in r4/phase1/5-merchant-voice.md PAIN-06 shows the pattern). Guard: park the order with an attention state when Allegro reports a productSet whose total product quantity is not 1 and the mapped variant has no definition. This guard is the one place the pilot reads `productSet`, as a three-state field used only as a check.
Old single-offer MULTIPACK promotion lines (before 2027-01-12) carry `discounts[{type: UNIT_PERCENTAGE_DISCOUNT}]` and must keep parsing (r5/1-allegro-pl.md C-005).

channelData.Allegro: `offer.productSet.products` with one element `quantity` N; line `quantity` counts packs and `price` is per pack (verify/allegro-line-price.md Q2); offer `stock.available` counts packs; replaces single-offer MULTIPACK from 2027-01-12 (C-005, r4/phase1/1-allegro.md ALG-02). Whether the order line always carries `productSet` for a multipack is unverified (r5/1-allegro-pl.md C-001 caveat c).

name: Freeze bundle contents per order
trigger: The first ingestion of an order whose line resolves to a bundle variant.
preconditions: B-04 recognition succeeded (order is ready, not `awaiting_mapping`).
mainFlow: Core computes the expansion from the current definition: component variant, quantity per set, quantity for the line.

Core writes it once, in the first ready transaction, into its own table with insert-if-absent: every evaluated line id (including lines that are not bundles, as a negative fact), bundle variant id, component productId and variantId, quantity per set, definition version, component catalogue gross prices (verify/standard-stress-test.md A2, C; verify/component-line-id.md surprises 5-6).
The recipe is merged per component variant before it is frozen, so no component id repeats (verify/component-line-id.md surprise 4).
Every later reader (reservation, routing, decrement, bench label, guards) reads the frozen expansion, never the live definition.
The `orderSnapshot` column is not touched (it stays the channel original, #3542).
altFlows: Re-poll after a definition edit: the insert is a no-op, the first expansion wins.

A definition created after the order was first evaluated: the negative fact keeps the line unexpanded, so holds and work stay on the bundle line id and are not duplicated (verify/standard-stress-test.md A2).

The operator remaps the line from kit X to plain Y after the freeze: the expansion check `frozen.bundleVariantId === item.variantId` fails, an attention is raised and the line is not routed (verify/standard-stress-test.md A2).
The order goes ready -> awaiting_mapping -> ready: the expansion row must survive (the ADR-080 cost snapshot does not, r5/6-design-and-code.md section 3.9).
An old order ingested late (backfill, reconcile) is frozen with the definition current at ingestion, not at sale (r5/2-shops-erp.md section 2).

name: Documents: one bundle line or component lines; mixed VAT
actor: System (invoice and receipt mappers); operator; tax adviser
trigger: A sales document is issued for an order with a bundle line.
preconditions: The order contains a recognised bundle line.
mainFlow: Pilot: the invoice and receipt mappers keep the bundle line as the channel sold it, with its own price and rate (D3, order-to-issue-invoice-command.mapper.ts:374,384).
Pilot: if component rates differ from the bundle rate, the definition carries a warning (B-01); nothing changes on the document.

Later: an operator setting per connection (or per bundle) chooses "one line" or "components", in the ADR-082 shape. Default split: proportional to each component own standalone gross selling price at the time of sale, frozen with the order and reused for refunds and corrections; an operator in-set price is an override with a recorded reason (verify/bundle-price-split.md sections 3-4). A component share above its own selling price raises a warning; capping is not an accepted method on its own (BFH XI R 22/22, r5/8-tax-fiscal.md C-035).
altFlows: A component line would carry 0.00 alone in its VAT bucket on eparagony: HTTP 400 errorCode 41 before the printer (C-028, verify/eparagony-gift-forms.md).

A single composite supply: one rate applies even when component prices are identifiable (ECJ C-463/16, r5/3-marketplaces-countries.md C-035), so "default to components when rates differ" (D3c) is not always right.

The bundle costs more than the sum of its standalone prices: a proportional split puts every component above its own price; no source covers this, flag for the adviser (verify/bundle-price-split.md section 4).

A component has no standalone selling price: the MF notice allows cost as the basis; the operator-recorded net unit cost (#3588) is a candidate but is net and optional (verify/bundle-price-split.md section 4).

name: The master already moves stock for a pack sale; avoid double or missing decrement
actor: System (order sync to a destination, master-absorbed holds)
trigger: An order containing a bundle is created in, or sold by, the product master itself.
preconditions: A bundle definition exists and the master is also the destination or the source.
mainFlow: Own-shop order (PrestaShop or WooCommerce selling its own pack): not routed (#3487); the shop decrements per its own pack rules (PrestaShop `StockManager.php:65-95`).

Mirror path: OL creates the order in the master; PrestaShop answers "does not lower stock" for any order with a pack (prestashop-order-stock-effect.resolver.ts:200-208), so OL keeps its holds until dispatch (under-sell, never oversell).
For WooCommerce and Shoper the answer is per order, not per line (C-059).

After the create, the post-sale master stock refresh and `consumeAbsorbedHolds` take `productIds` from `order.items` (order-sync.service.ts:443, :515), i.e. the bundle product: component holds stay held (under-sell, safe) and component stock is not refreshed from the master until the next sweep (verify/component-line-id.md section 3 site 8).
Pilot: a pinning spec asserts that `consumeAbsorbedHolds` never consumes holds on component positions (order-sync.service.ts:515, master-absorbed-reservation.service.ts:106-107, 207-208).
Pilot: definition warning when the bundle variant is a master kit (B-03).
altFlows: OL bundle defined on a plain master product (own counter): the master lowers only the bundle row; components are never lowered there (r3/code/C-stock-fulfilment-masters.md F4, F7).
Later: a line-grain stock-effect answer (`OrderCreateLineStockEffect`) once a second adapter needs it.

name: NEW Routed sale decrement of a master pack writes only the pack row (silent oversell)
trigger: An OMS-routed order (for example from Allegro) is for a variant that is a PrestaShop pack whose stock comes from components.
preconditions: OMS routing on; the line resolves to a PrestaShop pack in mode components or both; no OL bundle definition needed.
mainFlow: The sale decrement calls `adjustInventory(-n)` on the pack product (inventory-sale-decrement.service.ts).

Stage 0 fix (recommended): the PrestaShop adapter detects a pack whose stock comes from components (`readPackDefinition` + `resolvePackStockMode`, prestashop-inventory-master.adapter.ts:374-390) and refuses before writing with a typed error.
The sale decrement records the line as `blocked` and raises `stock-decrement-blocked` attention.
The operator corrects stock by hand or the client confirms the M option (decrement components like `validateOrder`).
altFlows: Pack-only mode (type 0): the pack row is the truth; the write is correct and allowed (verify/prestashop-live.md Q5).
Both mode (type 2): the write lowers the pack but standalone component offers keep selling; refuse as well, or decrement components (verify/prestashop-live.md Q5).

Type 3 (shop default) and the empty() read bug up to 9.1.5: the effective mode depends on the shop version, so a static rule can be wrong (verify/standard-stress-test.md A4, r5/2-shops-erp.md section 3).
Pack with no own row: already refused as absent records (visible) (r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md c4).
Return restock or manual correction on such a pack: same refusal, since the write is ignored by the shop (r5/2-shops-erp.md section 5).
Same question for a Shoper set or Subiekt komplet as master: unverified.

Live on 9.0.2: for `pack_stock_type=1` the PUT answered 200, wrote only the pack row, components and `Pack::getQuantity` did not change, and with the row at 0 a cart still accepted 5 packs; for type 0 the PUT takes effect; for type 2 it lowers availability via min(own row, components) but components are untouched; in no type did the PUT reach components (verify/prestashop-live.md Q5).

name: NEW Expand a bundle line into component lines for reservation, routing and sale decrement
trigger: An ingested order has a recognised bundle line with a frozen expansion.
preconditions: B-04 and B-10 done.
mainFlow: One pure function `expandFulfilmentLines(order, expansions)` returns one line per ordinary item with `orderLineId = item.id` (unchanged) and one per component with `orderLineId = {lineId}~c:{componentVariantId}`, quantity = per set x ordered.
Reservations use it (order-ingestion.service.ts:2236-2243).
Routing uses it through the shared projection (project-order-for-routing.ts:47-52), serving ingestion, dry run and the route handler.

The sale decrement handler builds its line map and `productId` from the same expansion, not from `orderItems`; the expansion must carry the component productId because of the `productVariantId === item.productId` rule (inventory-sale-decrement.handler.ts:90-117, verify/component-line-id.md surprise 5).

Six more sites keyed on the commercial line id must read the expansion or refuse: order-edit follow-ups `assessForEdit` and `lowerLineQuantity` (fulfillment-order-edit.service.ts:41-84), `narrowForOrder` (reservation.service.ts:247-261), `reverseLineQuantity` (inventory-sale-reversal.service.ts:155-200), the post-create stock refresh and absorbed-hold product ids (order-sync.service.ts:443, :515), and the return restock target (return-custody.service.ts:931-940). Nine sites in total, not three (verify/component-line-id.md section 4); the edit and restock sites are pilot guards (B-24, B-15).

Existing per-line keys (reservation index, closed-line gate, router conservation, work-line unique index, sale key, `closeForOrder`) become component-unique with no schema change; all columns are unbounded `text` and the longest key is about 185 of 255 characters (verify/component-line-id.md section 1).

Order items, snapshot, documents, shipment lines, return-line resolution, edit overlay and channel writebacks keep the bundle line. `shipment_lines` must stay on the bundle line: its coverage joins back to `orderSnapshot.items`, and component ids there would demote delivered orders (verify/component-line-id.md section 1 and surprise 3).
altFlows: Two components with the same variant cannot occur within one definition; a gift with the same variant later uses a reserved role segment `~g:` (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 4c).
An ambiguous component position: drop the whole bundle line, not one component (order-ingestion.service.ts:2281, r4/code/C-stock-flows-traced.md a2).

risks: The breaking-site count is about 25 (r4/code/B-line-identity-traced.md: 25 breaks, 7 safe, 4 unclear), not 6 as earlier rounds said.

Designs disagree: r5/7 derives ids only for fulfilment (`{lineId}~c:{variantId}`); r5/6 expands effective lines in `toDomain` with positional ids; r4/code/C uses `::` plus extra columns; r3/code/C threads a `componentKey` through routing. r5/7 rejects positional ids because they change when a definition is reordered.

Every missed site fails as a silent no-op, never a throw (`unrouted`, `not-applicable`, "NOT lowered" with outcome ok), so tests must assert the effect, not the absence of errors (verify/component-line-id.md surprise 1).

r5/7 named three call sites; verify/component-line-id.md finds nine. r4/code/C instead adds `parentOrderLineId` / `quantityPerBundle` columns; the column-free design works only if every reader goes through the expansion table (verify/standard-stress-test.md D9).
The id format is the expensive lock-in: it is persisted in terminal reservations, unique decrement keys and work lines (r5/7-scope-overengineering.md section 7.1).

name: NEW Operator edits or cancels an order that contains a bundle line
trigger: The operator lowers the quantity of a bundle line or cancels the order.
preconditions: Component-grain holds and work lines exist (B-23).
mainFlow: Quantity edit of a bundle line: refused with a new code `LINE_IS_BUNDLE` (pilot guard).

Whole-order cancel: holds of the order are released by order, which covers component holds; component stock comes back through `reverseForOrder`, which is row-based (inventory-sale-reversal.service.ts:117-150). But the cancellation stock restore republishes only the bundle own offers, not the component offers (offer-stock-restore.service.ts:350, 532-546, verify/component-line-id.md section 3).
Pilot: after a cancel, component offers are republished through the reverse fan-out of B-02 rather than a change to the restore service.
Discount edit on a bundle line: restates the bundle line price as for any line (documents keep the bundle line).
altFlows: Later: a bundle-line quantity edit scales component cancellations, hold narrowing and edit reversals by quantity per set.
